quotes.text: What slows organizations down is rarely governance itself, but rather the presence of immature governance. It's the kind of governance that depends on memory or heroic intervention from a few key people.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the 'governance slows us down' belief as a maturity problem.

quotes.text: In the world of Microsoft 365 and Copilot, AI does not invent new permissions. It simply inherits the ones you already have.

quotes.text: A template isn't just a shortcut, it is compressed governance. It takes 10 small decisions and resolves them once properly, so teams don't have to renegotiate them under pressure.

quotes.text: Citizen development doesn't create governance problems. It just scales them until they are impossible to ignore.

quotes.text: Governance is not just a form of risk management. It is a structural form of margin protection.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Immature governance, not governance itself, slows organizations down; designing a governed default path makes the safe route the fastest one.
A four-part readiness test of data, identity, control and outcome shows quickly whether a Copilot or Power Platform rollout is ready to scale.
Mature governance pays off as faster delivery, shorter AI time to value and reusable trust, which matters even more once autonomous agents take action.
hook: Many leaders still treat governance as overhead that slows innovation, until a Copilot or Power Platform rollout stalls on messy permissions and unclear ownership. This episode is for executives and IT leaders who want to turn governance into architecture, using a real services-firm case and a 15-minute readiness test to gain speed, trust and AI value.
